subject: ventures/hardwood-refinishing-bid-calculator
professional: an owner-operator or estimator at a floor-refinishing company (NWFA-style sand-and-finish and screen-and-recoat work) who bids jobs weekly and knows their own loaded crew cost, finish coverage and production rates

evidence.correctness: Ran calculateBid (node scratch script, not committed) on the page defaults (800 sq ft field, 12 treads, 2 closets, full sand, 3 coats, no stain, furniture 3 h, repair 1.5 h, $42 wage, 30% burden, $185 travel, 15% overhead, 25% margin) and recomputed independently in a second script that does not import calc.mjs. (1) Hours: 800/100*8=64 + 12*0.4=4.8 + 2*1 + 3 + 1.5 = 75.3 h; tool 75.3. Finish area 800+12*4=848 sq ft; gallons ceil(848*3/450)=ceil(5.65)=6; tool 6. Labor 75.3*42*1.3=$4,111.38; materials 6*85 + 8.48*18 = $662.64; direct 4,111.38+662.64+185=4,959.02; x1.15 = $5,702.87 cost; /0.75 = $7,603.83 price, $9.50/field sq ft. All matched to the cent, and matched the README and how-much-to-charge page figures. (2) Hallway preset (250 sq ft, 14 treads, stain, 1+1 h extras): finish area 306, hours 36.78, 3 finish gal + 1 stain gal, price $3,599.92 (stain on, 0 extra coats); matched the hand recompute. With 1 extra coat: hours rise from 33.11 to 36.78, price $3,907.34, matched hand arithmetic (the extra-coat hours 1.2*3.06 are included, gallons ceil(306*4/450)=3). (3) Screen living room preset: 400/100*3.5=14+2+0.5=16.5 h; $900.90 labor; 2 gal*85 + 4*18 = $242; cost $1,527.09; price $2,036.11; matched. Margin-on-price (cost/(1-m)) is the correct convention for a quoted price. Coverage compared to practice: 450 sq ft/gal/coat for finish is at the conservative end of manufacturer ranges (about 450-600 sq ft/gal/coat for waterborne and oil poly), so gallon counts err high, which is the safe direction. Departure: screen-and-recoat plus 'Stain' is priced without complaint ($5,745.15 for 800 sq ft + 12 treads, screen, stain): a floor with an existing finish cannot be stained without a sand, so that combination should be refused or forced to full sand.
evidence.completeness: README and page claims checked: field/tread/closet takeoff, screen vs full sand presets, stain and color-change presets, extra coat hours and gallons, loaded wage, overhead, margin price, price per field sq ft, walk-away price, proposed-price margin check, copy bid summary (formatBidSummary in calc.mjs), printable customer proposal with deposit and price-held date (proposal.mjs, 20 KB), share link in the URL hash (share.mjs), opt-out local usage tally (usage.mjs, 6 events), 3 SEO/comparison pages, llms.txt, sitemap, robots. All have code and tests; no stubs or TODOs found. Declared limitations (one currency, one house, one blended labor rate, ballpark starting hours) are honestly stated in the README. VENTURE.yaml stage is 'prototype' with all three hypotheses 'untested'.
evidence.verification: Ran `cd ventures/hardwood-refinishing-bid-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 102 tests, 102 pass, 0 fail, about 0.3 s. Seeded mutation 1 in calc.mjs: price = totalCost/(1 - margin) changed to totalCost/(1 + margin); result 98 pass, 4 fail (price stacking, proposed-price scoring, default range, worked-example figures), so the suite caught it. Mutation 2: Math.ceil -> Math.floor in gallonCount; 97 pass, 5 fail, caught. Both reverted with git checkout (git status for the directory clean). Gap: the pinned expected values are the author's own outputs, not figures from an outside source, and the page tests are string and structure checks, not a browser run.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs in full (304 lines) and the relevant parts of index.html, usage.mjs and the tests. Pure functions, no DOM or network, a single validating number() helper that throws on non-finite or below-min input, frozen presets, comments that say why, JSDoc on calculateBid. Defects: (a) STAIR_SQ_FT_PER_TREAD is a constant 4 and stairMaterialSqFt's per-tread parameter is not exposed in the UI or calculateBid, so a wide stair run cannot be corrected; (b) stain gallons are rounded up per job, and finish and stain are not pooled with leftover cans or sold sizes (1 vs 5 gal), which is fine but undisclosed; (c) METHOD_PRESETS and STAIN_PRESETS are independent, so invalid combinations (screen + stain) are reachable; (d) index.html is a 48 KB single file with inline script, hard to review; (e) hours-per-tread is a flat 0.4 whatever the stair width or whether risers are painted.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'no network calls, no accounts' (usage stored in localStorage key hardwood-refinishing-bid-usage only, per usage.mjs; opt-out and DNT/GPC respected per usage.test.mjs); disclaimer present on the page footer and in the README, with a separate proposal disclaimer; usage tracking present and described. Unbacked or wrong claims: (1) vs-a-flat-price-per-square-foot.html describes the $3,599.92 hallway as 'stain color change' but that figure is the preset with plain stain (extraCoats 0); the real color-change price is $3,907.34. (2) README and how-much-to-charge page say the same house as sand-and-stain 'is several hundred dollars more'; the tool prices it $9,019.73 vs $7,603.83, i.e. $1,416 more, so the claim is understated by a factor of about three. (3) llms.txt links four URLs on duncan-haywood.github.io, the retired Pages address, while README and VENTURE.yaml give marisstella.app. (4) vs-jobber.html says, in public prose and in its FAQ JSON-LD, 'Jobber's own site is not reachable from this session', which leaks agent-session wording onto a customer-facing page; the Jobber description itself is hedged, generic, carries no prices, and has an affiliation disclaimer, so there is no false competitor claim, but it lists 'flooring' among Jobber's trades without a source. (5) The FAQ 'a color change adds a whole extra coat... covering an existing color evenly typically takes one more pass' is not how refinishers do it: changing colour needs the old stain sanded out, not a thicker finish.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: an estimator enters 800 sq ft, 12 treads, 2 closets, full sand; gets price, per-sq-ft, hours split, walk-away price, a copyable summary and a printable proposal with deposit and valid-until date. That is a real and useful flow and the stairs/closets split is the right insight. Where a professional stalls in the first hour: one blended crew wage (no sander plus helper split), no multi-day or cure-time scheduling, no allowance for board repair/replacement beyond a flat hours input, no baseboard/shoe-mold or trim, no species/hardness or wide-plank factor, no dustless-system choice beyond a flat dollar input, no sales tax on materials, no per-room breakdown, and the starting production rates are not sourced. The tool does not stop invalid method/stain combinations. Proposal and share link are real extras.
evidence.domain: Compared against NWFA guidance as generally practised: full sand = rough/medium/fine passes, then stain, then 2-3 coats with a screen between; screen-and-recoat = abrade and 1-2 coats on a sound existing finish, no colour change. The structure (field hours, per-tread and per-closet hours, finish gallons from area x coats / coverage, labor burden, overhead, margin on price) is the standard estimating model. Departures: (1) stain on a screen-and-recoat is allowed; (2) the colour-change 'extra coat' replaces the extra sanding pass that actually drives cost; (3) 8 h/100 sq ft for a full sand with 3 coats (about 12.5 sq ft per crew-hour) reads high versus common crew production but is user-editable and sample-labelled; (4) no allowance for stain dry time or finish cure between coats; (5) 4 sq ft tread plus riser is plausible for a 36 inch stair (about 4.4) but fixed. A senior refinisher would use it for the stairs/closets split and the margin-on-price arithmetic, and reject the method/stain logic as written.

defects.what: Screen-and-recoat combined with Stain (or colour change) is priced without a warning ($5,745 for 800 sq ft + 12 treads); a finished floor cannot be stained or colour-changed without a full sand, so the quote would be physically unperformable at that price.

Colour change is modelled as one extra finish coat, and the page FAQ explains it as 'one more pass to cover the existing colour'. In practice colour change costs an extra sanding pass; the extra finish coat is the wrong cost driver.
README and how-much-to-charge page say sand-and-stain 'is several hundred dollars more'; the tool gives $1,416 more ($9,019.73 vs $7,603.83) for the same house.
vs-a-flat-price-per-square-foot.html labels the $3,599.92 hallway figure 'stain color change', but that figure is the plain-stain preset; the color-change price is $3,907.34.

vs-jobber.html says 'Jobber's own site is not reachable from this session' in customer-facing prose and FAQ JSON-LD, leaking agent-session wording; it also lists flooring among Jobber's trades without a source.
llms.txt links four URLs to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address instead of marisstella.app.
Stair square footage per tread is a fixed constant that the UI cannot change, and starting production rates (8 h/100 sq ft, 0.4 h/tread) are not sourced.

verdict: Arithmetic is right and checks out to the cent against an independent recompute (800 sq ft default $7,603.83, hallway $3,599.92, screen preset $2,036.11), the 102 tests pass, and two seeded bugs (margin sign, ceil to floor) were caught by 4 and 5 tests. It is finished: every README feature, including the proposal and share link, has working code. It does not meet the bar because claims scores 2: several public figures and labels are wrong or stale (sand-and-stain 'several hundred' dollars more is $1,416; the hallway is mislabelled colour change; llms.txt points at a retired host; vs-jobber leaks 'this session' wording), and the domain model lets a refinisher price an impossible job (stain on screen-and-recoat) and treats colour change as an extra finish coat rather than extra sanding. The worst defect is the method/stain model: a quote a practitioner could not perform at the price shown. All defects are cheap to fix; none was fixed here.
